title: Handley Page Hampden P4313
cause_of_loss: Flew into high ground near Ballaragh Farm House
memorial_details: Rectangular grey slate tablet with inscription in white lettering in relief below engraving of Royal Air Force badge.
inscription: IN MEMORY OF/ SERGEANT DOUGLAS BARCLAY - PILOT/ SERGEANT JOHN CASE - NAVIGATOR/ SERGEANT FRANK HANKINS - WIRELESS OPERATOR/AIR GUNNER/ WHO DIED HERE ON 27TH MARCH 1941 IN/ THE CRASH OF A HANDLEY-PAGE HAMPDEN/ OF THE RAF WHILST ON A TRAINING FLIGHT/ ERECTED BY/ THE MANX AVIATION PRESERVATION SOCIETY
narrative: On 27 March 1941, Hampden P4313 (D1) of 14 Operational Training Unit departed RAF Cottesmore at 10:15 on a cross-country navigation exercise. The aircraft flew into high ground near Ballaragh Farm House on the Isle of Man. Three crew members were killed; one was seriously injured. The slate tablet memorial, erected by the Manx Aviation Preservation Society, is mounted on the farm building wall at Ballaragh.
community_connection: The memorial was erected by the Manx Aviation Preservation Society and is mounted on the wall of Ballaragh Farm, at the site where the aircraft struck the hill. A fourth crew member survived seriously injured.

sources.title: Facebook post by Tony Hibberd (admin, RAF Bomber Command Memorials group), citing Chorley BCL Vol 7; photo by Jonathan Oliver
